title: Myanmar's war closes in on Sittwe, home of India-built port, as Arakan Army turns to Mizoram trade
dek: Junta airstrikes have killed at least 13 civilians in Rakhine this week, according to the Arakan Army and residents, as fighting spreads around Sittwe. The rebel group has signed a deal with a Mizoram transport body to formalise cross-border trade.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Fighting between Myanmar's military government and the Arakan Army is closing in on Sittwe, the capital of Rakhine State and the site of a port India built as the sea gateway of its Kaladan transport corridor from Kolkata to Mizoram. Junta aircraft have carried out a series of strikes across Rakhine this week that the Arakan Army and local residents say have killed at least 13 civilians.

With the junta blockading Rakhine by land and sea, the Arakan Army's political wing has meanwhile moved to put its trade with India on a firmer footing, signing an agreement with a vehicle owners' association in Mizoram's Saiha district on standard freight rates and daily border crossings.

## What happened

In the deadliest attacks, on 1 November, jets and Y-12 transport aircraft struck four Rakhine townships, killing 12 civilians and wounding 32, according to a statement from the Arakan Army. Seven travellers were killed when a jet bombed a bridge in Kyauktaw township at about 5.25 pm, and five people, including a newborn baby, were killed two minutes later when cluster bombs fell near a temporary clinic and maternity ward in Mrauk-U, reports said, citing residents. Other strikes that day hit Pauktaw town and a village in Kyaukphyu township, wounding 16. Late on 5 November, a jet bombed a village near a pagoda in Mrauk-U township, killing a pregnant woman and injuring 12 people, residents told reporters. "Our village has no military presence," one said.

The junta has not commented on the strikes, and the casualty figures cannot be independently verified. The military has previously said its air operations target armed groups it calls terrorists. Data from the Myanmar Internet Project cited in reports counted 581 airstrikes across Myanmar in the past three months, 151 of them in Rakhine, the most of any region.

On the ground, the Arakan Army said on 30 October that junta offensives on the Sittwe front in September and October had caused "severe and continuous clashes", with fighting near villages around the city and close to the military's regional command headquarters in Sittwe. Both sides have suffered significant casualties in battles on Ngapyi Island in Pauktaw township since the junta landed about 200 troops there on 7 October, reports said; neither side gives figures. "We still can't say for sure which side has the upper hand," an Arakan Army source said.

## The Mizoram deal

The agreement, signed on 29 October in Saiha, Mizoram, between the United League of Arakan and Arakan Army (ULA/AA) and the local branch of the Mizoram Commercial Vehicle Owners' Association, sets standard rates for trucks and boats. Border trade points at Rali and Salachwa on the Kaladan river are to open daily until 8 pm. A halt in trade in mid-September lasted more than a week. A trader said the deal would make trade "more formalized", preventing sudden disruptions. A ULA delegation also met Mizoram traders and officials on 29 and 30 October, reports said. India's government has not commented on the agreement.

## Why it matters for India

The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project was designed to link Kolkata's port by sea to Sittwe, then by river and road through Paletwa in Myanmar's Chin State to Mizoram, giving the north-east a route to the sea that avoids the narrow Siliguri corridor in north Bengal. The Sittwe port began operating in 2023, but the road link has been held up for years, and much of the route now runs through territory the Arakan Army controls. The fighting around Sittwe, and the rebels' growing trade ties with Mizoram, mean that any use of the corridor depends on dealings with both the junta and the Arakan Army.

The fighting also touches China's interests. Kyaukphyu township, hit by strikes on 1 November, hosts a Chinese-backed deep-sea port and special economic zone and the start of oil and gas pipelines to China's Yunnan province. Further north, armed fighters of the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) have been sighted in Arakan Army-held areas near the Bangladesh border, raising fears of renewed violence in an area from which hundreds of thousands of Rohingya have fled to Bangladesh, reports said.

## What happens next

The junta, which plans by-elections for 55 vacant seats on 4 April 2027, is trying to hold Sittwe and Kyaukphyu, its last major footholds in Rakhine. The Arakan Army controls most of the rest of the state.
